name: Post-employment sensitive-data theft and extortion sequence

attribution.legal_posture: Government threat reporting supplies the cited account; Swiss prosecution and named-person attribution fall outside the cited reporting.

caveats: Victim data and operational selectors stay unpublished.
This record is defensive behavior and geographic context only; named person, employer, facilitator, account, image, wallet, and adjudicated-outcome profiles require separate sources.
Use behavior-first wording; sequence coverage varies by case.

statements: Swiss federal cyber reporting describes a progression from deceptive hiring to theft of sensitive company data and extortion through threatened publication or sale. The defensible sequence is: obtain employment-derived access, collect sensitive data, then use threatened disclosure or sale to demand payment.
limitations: Government threat reporting, not a public Swiss prosecution or attribution to a named person.
The European government source describes post-hire data theft followed by extortion; this sequence does not identify an additional incident.
Use behavior-first wording; do not imply the sequence occurs in every case.
Do not publish victim data or operational selectors.
